$TTD just had one of the sharpest de‑ratings in its history.

Stock is down ~60–65 percent over 12 months and now trades around 30 dollars in PM with a ~13 billion dollar market cap, near multi‑year lows.

Fundamentals are not “broken,” but the growth narrative definitely is.

2025 revenue: 2.896 billion dollars, up 18 percent vs 2024’s 26 percent.

Q4 2025: 847 million dollars, +14 percent reported, ~19 percent excluding political spend.

The real shock was the outlook.

Q1 2026 revenue guidance: at least 678 million dollars, implying only ~10 percent YoY growth and ~500 bps margin compression.

That is a big step down from 25 percent+ growth just a year ago.

The market did what it always does with former high‑multiple names: it crushed the multiple.

TTD’s price‑to‑sales has collapsed from >20x in 2024 to roughly 4–5x today.

Trailing P/E is around 27x at an ~11.6–12 billion dollar market cap.

Enter the CEO.

On March 2–4, Jeff Green (via a limited partnership) bought 6,000,000 Class A shares in the open market at roughly 23.5–25.1 dollars.

Ticket size: about 148 million dollars. Largest insider stock purchase in company history.

Important context: for years, Green mainly sold stock at much higher prices (80–120 dollars+).

Flipping from consistent selling to a 9‑figure open‑market buy at 20‑something is a very loud signal about what he thinks of this reset.

On top of that, he received ~398k restricted shares and options on ~737k shares with a 25 dollar strike.

His economic exposure is now heavily skewed to whether TTD can compound from this level over the next 3–5 years.

So what is the real story?
Bull case: TTD is still the dominant independent DSP in open‑internet ads, CTV and retail media are long‑run tailwinds, the Kokai platform migration is done, and 18–20 percent+ growth plus high FCF returns, making 4–5x sales too cheap.

Bear case: we are seeing the new normal.
Macro pressure in CPG and autos (more than a quarter of the business) drags on budgets, walled gardens keep tightening, growth sticks around 10–15 percent and margins sag as TTD invests heavily in AI and infrastructure.

My read: the risk/reward finally looks interesting.
TTD moved from “priced for perfection” to “priced like a normal ad tech name,” exactly when the founder‑CEO just bought 6 million shares at the lows.

If they can re‑accelerate above mid‑teens growth, today will likely look cheap.

Not advice, but if you passed on TTD at 80–120 dollars because of the nosebleed multiple, you are now looking at the same asset, lower growth, lower multiple and much higher insider conviction.

The question is simple: do you believe this is a slowdown or a reset.
